newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures turn up after mixed start.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures turn up after mixed start.

text.p: CME lumber futures ranged mixed early with pressure coming from an easier undertone to cash spruce but futures moved up early on short covering prompted by the discount to cash, traders said.

Although cash lumber is looking weaker, futures are currently well below the cash equivalent which prompted some support. Futures are trading as if cash was down at $350 per tbf and not the $355 quote, sources said.
Evening of positions ahead of the weekend also provided support after initial pressure, traders said.
The cash spruce market will have to show a break in prices before futures can move much lower, they said.

Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $355 per tbf, unchanged from midweek and up $3 from last Friday. Some producers openly admitted they would be forced to drop prices by next week if sales didn't pick up, but others claimed order files into September, they said.
At 0940 CDT, lumber futures were $2.10 to $1.20 per tbf higher with September up $1.50 at $346.50 and November up most at $345.70 per tbf.
